title: Prospecting & Business Development Foundations
description: Week 2 moves participants from sending messages to building a system that books conversations. They define ideal contact profiles, research and qualify prospects, and map 2-3 contacts inside each priority employer-partner organization; A/B test message variants against real reply data and adapt tone and ask by audience; and convert replies into scheduled conversations, conducting structured 20-minute informational interviews. Weekly milestone: 2+ conversations booked; first informational interview completed and debriefed.
notes: Weekly milestone: 2+ conversations booked; first informational interview completed and debriefed.
lesson_length: Lab-guide lessons, roughly 1200-1800 words each, supporting a full week of live instructor-led practice
learning_objectives: Define ideal contact profiles and qualify prospects, mapping multiple contacts per priority organization
A/B test message variants against real reply data and adapt tone and ask by audience
Convert replies into scheduled conversations and run structured informational interviews

lessons.title: Target Research & List Building
objectives: Define ideal contact profiles and qualify prospects, mapping multiple contacts per priority organization
Map 2-3 contacts inside each priority employer-partner organization

lessons.title: Messaging Craft & Testing
objectives: A/B test message variants against real reply data and adapt tone and ask by audience
Adapt tone, length, and the size of the ask to the recipient and relationship stage

lessons.title: Booking & Running Informational Interviews
objectives: Convert replies into scheduled conversations and run structured informational interviews
Conduct a structured 20-minute informational interview and debrief it into actionable intelligence

sequencing_rationale: Week 2 moves from sending to a system that books conversations. Target research precedes messaging because message quality depends on knowing the audience; interviews come last because they consume the replies the first two lessons generate. Scope assumption: A/B testing is taught against real reply data at novice scale (small samples, directional reads), not statistical significance.
